not_escrowed_because: Superseded. This signer held none of the payment token and this said nothing had been spent to change that. Something was: the operator bought 0.2058 of it on PancakeSwap v2 (0x63a1b95c…78f2) and escrowed 0.1 into job 56681 on mainnet. Chapel still did not escrow, which is what this record is about.
not_escrowed_because_was: This signer holds none of the payment token, and nothing has been spent to change that: it is owner-minted with no faucet, but it **trades on PancakeSwap** against USDT at about 0.9996 — so the escrow is a purchase away rather than out of reach. `fund()` also refuses a zero budget outright (`ZeroBudget()`, `0xff97b861`). `createJob` and `setBudget` are real transactions on a real deployment; `fund` is not among them, and this field is why rather than an omission. The funded flow runs to settlement on a mainnet fork — see the fork proof below.
success_criterion: The position was in range for at least 70% of samples over the job window, recomputed from chain state. Binary, and it needs no counterfactual — spec section 4.2, gap item G-3.

transactions.meaning: registerJob reverts on a job created with the router as its hook, for every policy argument tried including the OptimisticPolicy the deployment publishes. Name unresolved. The behaviour is consistent with the hook having registered the job already, which would make step 3 of erc8183.steps() a no-op on this deployment — but that is an inference from a revert, and nothing here has read a registration back out to confirm it
